guards: Two QT-prolonging agents carry an additive torsades risk that neither medication's own row shows and no single-drug check can see - the flag exists precisely because the danger is in the pair. Guards the two-drug threshold, which is what separates a useful flag from one that fires on every antiarrhythmic a cardiology panel is full of.

answer.intent: Seeded violation of FR-VERIF-2's QT-prolonging drug combination constraint: amiodarone and sotalol are concurrently active, which is two class III antiarrhythmics on one list.
